2  CRL.P No. 100232 of 2023  C/W CRL.P No. 101506 of 2023  THESE CRIMINAL PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI  ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI)

Petitioner in Crl.P.No.100232/2023 is the wife and she is seeking transfer of CC No.23/2022 on the file of the Civil Judge and JMFC, Mundgod,
Uttara Kannada to the Court of JMFC, Nippani, Belagavi District, for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 323, 342, 504 and 506 of IPC.
2. Petitioner in Crl.P.No.101506/2023 is the husband and he is seeking quashing of criminal proceedings initiated against him in the above case.
3. Since the facts giving rise to these petitions are same, they are clubbed together and disposed of by a common order.
For sake of convenience, the wife is referred to as complainant and husband is referred to as accused.

5. The complainant is seeking transfer of CC No.23/2022 from Mundgod to Nippani, contending that based on the complaint filed by her, the concerned police have filed charge sheet against her husband for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 323, 342, 504 and 506 of IPC.
5.1 After she left the matrimonial home, she is residing at Nippani.
The distance between Nippani and Mundgod is very long and it is very difficult for her to go there and give evidence.
Accused who is her husband is an aggressor and used to assault her mercilessly.
He is waiting to take revenge against her.

It is not safe for her to go to Mundgod to give evidence and hence, the petition.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:17906 6.
After due service of notice, accused has appeared through counsel and resisted the petition.
7. During the course of his arguments, learned counsel for the complainant submitted that Crl.Mis.24/2022 and execution petitions, filed by her are pending at Nippani Courts.
This Court has also transferred M.C.342/2021 filed by the accused from Mundgod to Nippani and CC No.23/2022 may also be transferred.

sentences.text: The complaint averments and the consequent charge sheet reveal that the marriage of petitioner and respondent was performed 12 years back.
Unfortunately, the complainant did not beget children.

She has alleged that because of this reasons, the accused is treating cruelly and on NC:
2024:KHC-D:17906 12.10.2021 she was assaulted by him.
This was witnessed by her neighbor.

10. On the other hand, it is alleged by the accused that the complainant stayed in the matrimonial home only for a period of one and half years and left the matrimonial home and staying in her parents house.
When he filed M.C. No.342/2021 for divorce, she has chosen to file a false complaint.
Of course, it is a matter for evidence for both parties to prove their respective contentions.
11. As per the charge sheet, the petitioner- wife is the complainant and victim.
CW.6 Gayathri is cited as eye witness.
Her brothers Rajendra Prasad and Dilip Kumar, who are cited as CWs.4 and 5 are not eye witnesses.

Apart from them, there are witnesses to the spot mahazar, the officials of Gram Panchayat who has issued NC: 2024:KHC-D:17906 property extract, the medical officer, head constable who has registered the case and P.S.I. who has conducted investigation and filed charge sheet are the prosecution witness.

12. The complainant and her brothers are required to appear before the Trial Court only once for their evidence and it would not be difficult for them to appear before the Trial Court and give evidence.
On the other hand, if the case is transferred to Nippani, all the other witnesses including the official witness would be put to difficulty.
The comparative inconvenience that would be caused to the complainant and her brothers is less than that which would be caused to the other witnesses.
The complainant has alleged that respondent husband was treating her cruelly when she was in the matrimonial home.
It may not NC: 2024:KHC-D:17906 be valid ground to transfer the said case from Mundgod to Nippani.
13. Now, coming to the petition filed by the accused-husband seeking quashing of criminal proceedings against him.

In support of his petition, the accused has contended that only after filing of divorce petition in M.C.342/2021, and its transfer, the complainant has chosen to file one after the other petitions under the provisions of Cr.P.C., Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act and under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act and also criminal complaint with ill motive.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 14. Without holding any preliminary enquiry, the concerned police have mechanically registered the case against him.

Except the self serving statement of the complainant, there is no material to connect the accused with the crime and continuation of the proceeding would amount to NC:
2024:KHC-D:17906 abuse of the process of the Court and pray to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him.
15. It is true that the complainant has chosen to file the complaint after the accused filed petition seeking divorce.
However, the complaint averments reveal that on the date of incident, the accused assaulted her.

She has also narrated that earlier to the incident also, he used to assault her,
especially for the reason that she could not bear children and demanded to get Rs.2,00,000/-.

sentences.text: According to the prosecution, CW.6 Gayatri is an eye witness.
CWs.2 and 3 are the spot mahazar witnesses.
Of course, CWs.4 and 5 who are the brothers of the complainant are not eye witnesses.
CW.8 Dr.Shrishma has examined the complainant and issued the injury certificate, according to which the injury suffered by - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:17906 complainant are simple in nature.

The entire material placed on record,
makes out a strong prima facie case against the accused.

The allegations made against him are required to be proved at a full fledged trial and it is not a case for quashing the proceedings and therefore, the petition filed by the accused is also liable to be dismissed and accordingly the following;
ORDER 1. Crl.P.No.100232/2023 filed by the wife is dismissed.
2. Petition filed by the accused-husband under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is also hereby rejected.
